newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell $50 mln T-bills to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell $50 mln T-bills to foreigners.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank plans to sell $50 million of Treasury bills to non-residents on the secondary market in the near future to raise its foreign currency reserves, a top bank official said on Monday.

"We must bring our reserves to $884 million, our basic level for operating reserves, and we'll have to make money through T-bill sales to get to that level," Mykola Melnychuk, chief of foreign currency reserves, told Reuters.
Operating reserves dipped below their regular level after the central bank issued a credit to the Finance Ministry.

Melnychuk did not specify the amount of the credit, but the ministry had hoped to repay it by the end of October with a 50 million Ecu credit from the European Commission and a World Bank credit of $100 million.
He said foreign investors would be able to buy bills directly from the central bank and not have to go through Ukrainian commercial banks.
Central bank officials said the bank would repay buyers in hard currency when the T-bills mature. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
